skills.name: Guided case study: BEAC as a central bank

note.text: BEAC is the common central bank for Cameroon, Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea and Chad. Its official description assigns monetary policy, currency issue, exchange policy, official foreign-exchange reserves, payments functioning and financial-stability responsibilities. Its role is regional rather than a separate central bank serving only Cameroon. The source also describes resources supplied to COBAC for banking supervision; this is not a reason to erase the institutions’ distinct roles. This exercise uses the official description, not current rates or a policy forecast.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to use an official institutional description to assign roles and avoid unsupported policy claims. Builds on: central-bank and fiscal distinctions. Leads to: public-finance foundations and later monetary analysis.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: Source-based classroom paraphrase, not a quotation: the official BEAC institutional page identifies a common central bank and its monetary responsibilities. In an invented sorting exercise, one card proposes a monetary-policy task, another names a government tax decision and a third describes a customer loan. Only the first directly matches the stated central-bank policy role. The exercise supplies no current reserve-ratio decision.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Record source, institution, scope and the claim actually supported. Sort each invented task by role, then explain the evidence. Mark absent figures as unknown. Confirm current applicable decisions from their own official documents rather than extracting them from a general mission page.

e: Mandate and outcome differ.
Outcome claims need measurement.
Lack of outcome evidence does not erase the role.
